title: Surface Tension and Excess Pressure

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Mechanical Properties of Fluids

expression: T = F/l ;  Excess pressure (drop) = 2T/r ;  Excess pressure (soap bubble) = 4T/r
explanation: Surface tension T is the force per unit length acting along a liquid surface, tending to minimise surface area. Because a spherical liquid drop has ONE surface, the excess pressure inside it is 2T/r; a soap bubble has TWO surfaces (inner and outer film surfaces), so its excess pressure is double that of a drop of the same radius, 4T/r. Smaller radius means larger excess pressure — a smaller bubble/drop has higher internal pressure than a larger one of the same liquid.

workedExample.scenario: A soap bubble of radius 1 cm, surface tension 0.03 N/m.

commonMistakes: Using the drop formula (2T/r) for a soap bubble — a bubble has two surfaces, so it needs the doubled formula 4T/r, a very common exam trap.
Assuming larger drops have higher internal pressure — smaller radius actually means HIGHER excess pressure (inverse relationship).
genZNote: Soap bubbles have double the surface drama — literally two surfaces, double the excess pressure.
